name: MCP server
description: `afterglow mcp`: a Model Context Protocol server over stdio that serves every app's command catalog as tools. MCPVersions pins the protocol revisions (2026-07-28 sessionless; 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 start with initialize); JSONRPC frames one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per line; MCPServer (with MCPOptions: apps, roots, limits) answers each line; MCPTools lists the tools and routes a tool name to an MCPRoute; MCPSessions holds the open documents by expiring handle and returns MCPToolResults. MC-4 builds the server: strict JSON-RPC parsing (-32700, -32600), version negotiation (-32602 listing supportedVersions), server/discover, initialize, ping, tools/list, rate-limited tools/call, silent notifications, and serve (`--app`, `--root`, `--live`) reading stdin line by line. MC-6 builds the tools: each app's open and new, then afterglow.save, export and close, then every command as <app>.<id> in id order with input {doc, params} and annotations from its kind. MC-8 builds the calls: open and new give a UUID handle and the summary ({doc, summary}), each command runs through the app's catalog ({result, undoStep?}), save and export write {path} only under the roots and never replace a file without force, close drops a handle; paths are checked by their real location (.. folded, every symlink resolved, the roots' own included); at most maxOpen handles, each expiring once idle for idleSeconds; why-nots, schema issues (each /path: message), refused paths and dead handles are tool errors (isError). MC-11 builds `--live` (macOS; refused with 69 elsewhere): LiveBridge finds the running apps' sockets (<app>-<pid>.sock under Application Support/AfterGlow/live), asks each for live/describe over LiveWire (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on a same-user Unix socket, UnixSocketLink), lists their commands as live.<app>.<id> with input {params}, skips a dead or garbled socket, and forwards each call as live/run with the client's name from initialize; an app's needsGrant answer (-32010) is the tool error "<App> asked you to approve this client", any other refusal the app's own words.
